note: New synthetic Phase III-I.5 scenarios. Expand to the flat candidate only when all 30 groups are complete.

groups.baseline: The clinic sends appointment reminders by email and SMS; the patient can choose either channel.
cases: Keep email reminders, but take texts off the menu altogether.
SMS is an explicit option being eliminated.
Keep email and text reminders, but send the texts two hours earlier.
Patients can still get email. They shouldn't be offered the phone-message option now.
The SMS choice disappears while email survives.
tiny correction from ops: email stays, txt reminders don't. booking itself is same.
Only the SMS reminder channel is withdrawn.
Could the reminder also go to the patient's portal inbox, without changing the existing channels?
Maybe we should rethink those reminders? The team hasn't settled what to do with email or texts.

groups.baseline: Visitors may enter with a printed ticket or a ticket stored in the museum app; guards verify either at the door.
cases: App tickets are fine; please retire paper admission at the door.
App and printed tickets should both work, though guards will scan them at the desk rather than the door.
Both options survive with a changed verification location.
The guards should stop taking the printed version, not the one in the app.
One named admission format is withdrawn.
Sorry, confusing note earlier. mobile pass yes; the printout no longer counts. door team unchanged.
The printout ceases to be accepted.
Keep checking both forms at entry; the sign explaining it could use friendlier wording.
Only signage copy changes, not ticket acceptance.
can we take a PDF pass too? not replacing paper or the app, just another way in
PDF is an additional ticket format.

groups.baseline: A warehouse sensor records freezer temperature every five minutes and displays readings in Celsius and Fahrenheit.
cases: Change the sampling interval to two minutes; don't change what the probe measures.
Existing sampling continues at a new frequency.
Keep the five-minute Celsius reading and also show a Fahrenheit conversion.
A new display option is added.
The freezer still needs a temperature point, only more often: every two minutes.
The interval changes, not the capability.
ops says 5 min feels laggy; make it 2. still Celsius, still the same probe.
Stop showing Celsius while retaining the temperature record in Fahrenheit.
The explicit Celsius display is removed.
maybe faster sampling? need to ask facilities what interval they actually want
No final interval or instruction is settled.

groups.baseline: The transcript portal must never show an unpublished grade to students; teachers may preview unpublished grades.
cases: Keep that privacy rule, but let students peek at grades before publication.
Student preview violates the explicit never invariant.
Let department heads preview unpublished grades as teachers already do; students still cannot.
A new authorized preview actor is added without violating the student ban.
A student preview link should work while the grade is still unpublished, even if it's read-only.
Read-only visibility still breaks the invariant.
i know it says never for students, but could we show them draft marks just for a minute? yes please ship that
A definite request violates the student-visibility prohibition.
Teachers can keep previewing drafts; publish the student-facing grades only when released.
The stated visibility boundary is preserved.
Can we revisit who sees the draft? not decided whether that means staff or pupils yet
The actor and decision are unresolved.

groups.baseline: Commuters can renew a monthly rail pass in the app or at a station kiosk before the pass expires.
cases: Leave renewal in the app, but drop kiosk renewals. The expiry rule stays.
The kiosk channel is explicitly eliminated.
Keep both renewal channels but allow renewal for two days after expiry.
Renewal survives with a changed time window.
Station kiosks will no longer renew passes; passengers still have the app before expiry.
quick one: the app route is good. kiosk renewal is out of scope now, not kiosk sales in general
Could riders also renew through the website while app and kiosk remain?
The website is an additional renewal channel.
The kiosk screen can have nicer colours, sure, but renewal still needs to work there and in-app before expiry.

groups.baseline: A manager must approve an employee expense over 500 dollars before finance pays it; employees may draft expenses without approval.
cases: Keep the manager gate, but pay an $800 claim first and get approval afterward.
Paying before required approval violates the invariant.
Require manager approval before payment for expenses over $400 rather than $500.
The approval gate remains with a new threshold.
For a claim above the limit, finance should release funds while the manager's decision is still pending.
hey, big reimbursements are taking ages. Can payroll send them now and chase the signoff later? yes, even the $900 ones
A definite post-payment approval request conflicts with the before invariant.
Let employees save drafts without manager involvement, then keep the pre-payment gate for large claims.
Existing draft and approval behavior are restated.
Could finance send a receipt after approved payouts? approvals still happen first of course
A receipt is added without changing the approval gate.

groups.baseline: The backup app saves original photos to local storage and to the user's cloud vault when both destinations are enabled.
cases: Keep the cloud copy, but remove the local copy from the backup flow.
Local storage is a named baseline destination being removed.
Keep both copies, but upload the cloud one overnight instead of immediately.
Both destinations survive with changed timing.
There should be no on-device backup file; the vault copy still happens.
phone storage is filling up. please cloud-only the backup; gallery display isn't what I'm asking to delete
Add an optional encrypted USB backup alongside the current two destinations.
A third backup destination is added.
what if we don't keep every copy? not sure which place we'd trim yet

groups.baseline: If a buyer opens a dispute, the platform emails both buyer and seller within one hour and keeps the dispute visible in the portal.
cases: The portal record stays, and sellers still get the email; buyers no longer need that email.
The buyer email is explicitly removed.
Email both parties within thirty minutes; keep the portal record.
Both notifications survive with a shorter deadline.
Skip only the buyer's dispute email, not the seller's or the portal entry.
One actor's notification capability is removed.
support clarified: no buyer mail on new disputes pls. seller gets theirs; portal page isn't going away
Buyer email is withdrawn while the other outputs persist.
Add a push alert for the buyer, while keeping both existing emails and the portal record.
A new notification channel is added.
Can we rename the dispute tab? no change to the emails, timing, or record itself

groups.baseline: Only workspace owners may revoke an API key; editors may view a key's last-used timestamp but must not see the secret value.
cases: Keep owners as revokers; editors should also be able to revoke stale keys.
Editor revocation violates the only-owners invariant.
Let editors export the last-used timestamps as CSV; secret values stay hidden.
A timestamp export is added without breaking the secret restriction.
An editor should be allowed to disable a compromised key immediately, even before an owner reviews it.
Editor disable/revocation conflicts with the exclusive owner permission.
in an incident the editor on call needs to kill the key. owner can be asleep; let's enable that role
The proposed editor revocation violates the owner-only invariant.
Keep secret values away from editors; last-used time is still visible to them.
Could the on-call person maybe get 'more control' over keys? we haven't decided which role or action

groups.baseline: Players may reserve a court for a 30-minute or 60-minute session; both durations appear in the booking picker.
cases: Make the half-hour slot unavailable. The hour slot is still bookable.
Keep both durations but start every reservation ten minutes later than the displayed slot time.
Both options remain with changed start timing.
People should only be offered the hour-long court session from now on.
small booking tweak: 30m is gone, 60m isn't. don't touch court inventory
Could we offer a 45-minute slot as well as the two existing lengths?
maybe drop a length? haven't picked which one, and maybe we'd keep both after all
No definite option removal is chosen.

groups.baseline: Readers can filter the catalogue by author or by subject; the filter panel works on desktop and mobile.
cases: Add language as another filter; don't replace author or subject.
Language is a new filter option.
Keep author and subject filtering on both devices; rename the panel heading.
Let readers narrow results by language too. The existing author and subject controls stay.
A third filtering facet is added.
Side note: the mobile header is cramped and design will fix it later. For this ticket, add a language facet, leave the old filters alone.
Irrelevant UI context does not alter the added filter.
Keep subject filtering, but stop offering author filtering on both desktop and mobile.
On both devices, author filtering goes away; subject filtering stays. sorry for the wordy note.
Clause order changes, not the removal.

groups.baseline: Payroll clerks may export the monthly pay register as CSV, and each export includes employee ID and net pay.
cases: Change the export cadence to weekly; CSV and both columns remain.
The existing export occurs more frequently.
Omit employee ID from the CSV; net pay and the export remain.
One explicit output field is eliminated.
Clerks still need the same CSV fields; generate the register every week instead of monthly.
Finance mentioned filenames too, but that's a separate ticket. This one is weekly CSV, same ID/net fields.
Filename context is irrelevant to a frequency modification.
Add gross pay as a third column, while preserving employee ID and net pay.
Keep ID and net pay, and put gross pay in there too. monthly CSV otherwise unchanged.
Clause order changes but the new field is the same.

groups.baseline: Riders unlock a bike with an app QR code, and a ride receipt appears in the app after the bike is returned.
cases: Show the same receipt immediately at unlock instead of at return; QR unlock still works.
Receipt timing changes while both capabilities survive.
Could receipts maybe happen earlier? We have not chosen when.
The receipt should arrive when the ride starts, not when it ends. Nothing about unlocking changes.
Receipt timing is set to the start.
QR scans are a little flaky but that's for another ticket. here: receipt at start of trip, not at dock-back.
QR commentary is irrelevant to a definite receipt-timing change.
Retain the QR unlock; discontinue the in-app ride receipt entirely.
The explicit receipt capability is eliminated.
No receipt in the app anymore, but leave the QR unlock alone pls.
Clause order does not alter removal of the receipt.

groups.baseline: A filing must be signed by the submitting lawyer before it is transmitted; clerks may preview the unsigned draft.
cases: Keep the signature rule, but transmit urgent unsigned filings and have counsel sign later.
Transmission before required signature violates the invariant.
Keep signatures before transmission; add a 24-hour reminder to the lawyer if the draft is still unsigned.
A reminder is added without relaxing the signing gate.
Urgent filings should go out before the lawyer signs, with signature collected afterward.
Clerks asked for bigger preview text, separate thing. For this one, send first, sign after if it's urgent.
UI detail distracts from an incompatible transmission order.
Counsel signs before sending; the clerk can still inspect an unsigned draft.
The signing and preview order is preserved.
Clerk preview is fine while unsigned; don't actually send until lawyer's signature is there.
Clause order differs but behavior is unchanged.

groups.baseline: Receiving staff record returned parcels and supervisors approve disposal; staff can place parcels in quarantine pending review.
cases: Supervisors still approve disposal, but take quarantine off the receiving team's options.
One explicit staff capability is removed.
Keep quarantine and disposal approval, but have staff record returns within two hours rather than at intake.
Return logging survives with changed timing.
The team may log returns as before; they must not park them in quarantine anymore.
we still need parcel logging and boss signoff. quarantine button is confusing though—please remove that workflow, not just the text
Let auditors view the disposal approval log, without altering staff or supervisor powers.
A read-only actor capability is added.
Staff and supervisor steps stay put; auditors can now read the disposal log. that's it.
Clause order leaves the additional auditor access intact.

groups.baseline: Customers may pay subscription invoices by card or bank transfer and can download a PDF receipt after settlement.
cases: Leave bank transfer in place; card payments should no longer be accepted for these invoices.
One explicit payment mechanism is removed.
Retain card and transfer, but make receipts available before settlement instead of after.
The receipt survives with changed timing.
The finance portal can still take transfers. Take the card route out of subscription checkout.
unrelated: receipt PDF typography needs love. actual change is no cards for subs; transfers okay.
The typography remark does not change the card removal.
Offer direct debit alongside the existing card and transfer routes; receipts stay as they are.
A third payment mechanism is added.
Keep the receipt thing and both current payment methods. Direct debit too, please.
Clause order leaves the additional payment method intact.

groups.baseline: A machine must not restart while its maintenance lock is engaged; operators may inspect status during lockout, and the status display refreshes every five seconds.
cases: Keep the lock indicator, but let a supervisor restart the motor before removing the maintenance lock.
Restart during lockout violates the explicit prohibition.
Keep restart blocked during lockout; refresh the status display every second instead of every five.
The existing display refresh interval changes.
While the lock remains engaged, a remote operator should be able to resume the machine.
Safety still owns the lock process; remote restart during a locked service window would save time. yes, enable it.
Context does not remove the lockout invariant.
Operators can inspect status during maintenance, and the machine stays stopped until unlocked.
The inspection and restart constraints remain.
while locked, show status to ops. no restart till lock is off, obviously.
Clause order and casual wording preserve the rule.

groups.baseline: New employees upload identity documents to the HR portal; HR officers verify them and employees can view the verification status.
cases: Let team leads see the status too; HR still verifies and employees still see their own status.
A new viewer role is added.
Keep HR as the verifier and employees as status viewers; change the portal heading to 'Onboarding'.
Keep the current identity workflow and expose status to the recruit's team lead as well.
Design also wants a new icon, but that's later. Main ask: lead can read status, not verify docs.
Icon commentary does not alter the added lead-view capability.
Employees should still upload documents, but remove their status view; HR verification remains.
HR still checks the ID and new hires still upload it. they just don't get to see the status anymore.
Clause order preserves the status-view removal.

groups.baseline: The utility dashboard shows daily water consumption in litres and lets households download a monthly CSV summary.
cases: Display the same daily amount in cubic metres; keep the monthly download.
The display unit changes while usage reporting survives.
End the monthly CSV download, but keep daily consumption on screen.
A named export capability is removed.
The daily chart is still there; express volume in m³ instead of L.
CSV isn't the issue. change the daily chart units to m3 so it matches bills, same measurements.
CSV context is irrelevant to the unit modification.
Add a weekly PDF digest without removing the daily chart or monthly CSV.
Daily chart + monthly CSV stay. also could we have a weekly PDF? yes that's the ask.
Clause order does not alter the added digest.

groups.baseline: Clinicians must obtain patient consent before recording a video visit; the consent prompt appears when the call begins, and patients may withdraw consent at any time to stop recording.
cases: Keep the consent banner, but begin recording before patients respond so we don't miss the greeting.
Recording before consent violates the explicit invariant.
Show the consent prompt during scheduling instead of at call start; recording still waits for consent.
The existing prompt moves earlier without weakening the consent rule.
Capture the start of the call, then ask permission to keep that footage.
No one is removing the opt-out, but the first 30 seconds need to be captured before they click yes. please do it.
Opt-out context does not cure pre-consent recording.
Recording starts only after consent; a later withdrawal ends it immediately.
The baseline order and withdrawal effect are restated.
If they back out, stop the video. and obviously don't record till they opt in.
Clause order preserves both consent rules.

groups.baseline: An assistant may schedule meetings up to 30 days ahead on an executive's calendar, while only the executive may cancel a confirmed meeting.
cases: Change the assistant's booking horizon to 45 days; confirmed cancellation stays with the executive.
The existing booking permission survives with a changed horizon.
Could the assistant have more control over confirmed meetings? We haven't specified which actions.
Somebody should be able to adjust a confirmed meeting. Not sure whether we mean time, venue, or cancellation.
The intended operation is not determined.
exec team also wants a nicer invite email, separate ticket. here they asked for 'more control' for assistants, but wouldn't say what that covers.
Email context cannot resolve the unspecified permission.
Only the executive cancels confirmed meetings; assistants still arrange new ones.
Assistants book the meetings; confirmed cancellations stay with the exec. yes that's still the rule.
Clause order does not alter permissions.

groups.baseline: A patient can request a repeat prescription through the portal; requests reach a pharmacist in a nightly batch, and the pharmacist reviews them before dispatch.
cases: Keep review before dispatch, but send refill requests from the portal to a pharmacist immediately rather than in the nightly batch.
The review path remains with changed routing time.
What if refills went faster? Nothing decided about which step yet.
The target and change are unspecified.
The clinic mentioned same-day refills but did not say whether that means review, dispatch, or delivery.
The operation to change is unresolved.
We also have a packaging redesign coming. for the refill flow they said 'speed it up somehow' and then left the call.
Packaging context does not settle the vague request.
Keep the pharmacist check before any medicine goes out, with portal requests still available.
The baseline review order and intake channel remain.
Request in portal, pharmacist checks, then dispatch. no shortcut to shipping first.
Clause order reiterates the baseline sequence.

groups.baseline: Creators can generate subtitles in English or Spanish and edit the subtitle text before publication.
cases: Keep both subtitle languages; support French too, but leave editing as-is.
A third language option is introduced.
Maybe we need another subtitle language; the team hasn't selected one or approved it.
No definite new language is chosen.
Creators should also be able to generate French captions, alongside English and Spanish.
French is an additional generation option.
Ignore last week's font debate. Product signed off on French captions as a third choice; editing still works.
Font context does not change the addition.
English and Spanish subtitle generation and pre-publication edits should stay.
Let them edit before posting; languages are still English and Spanish. nothing to change there.

groups.baseline: Fleet managers receive a service alert every 10,000 kilometres and can record completed service in a vehicle ledger.
cases: Set the alert at 8,000 km; recording completed service doesn't change.
Should we revisit the mileage interval? Nobody has picked a new figure.
The new threshold is not decided.
Managers keep getting a mileage alert, only at eight thousand rather than ten.
The existing alert persists with a changed threshold.
Ignore the oil-brand discussion from ops. Make the service ping 8k km, ledger stays put.
Oil context does not alter the threshold modification.
Keep the ten-thousand-kilometre alert and ledger entry for completed service.
Service still gets logged after it's done, and alert at 10k km as before. cheers.
Clause order and casual wording preserve the baseline.

groups.baseline: Field researchers upload a geotagged photo for each bird sighting to the survey portal.
cases: Add an optional audio clip to each sighting; keep the geotagged photograph.
An audio evidence option is added.
Could we include something else with sightings someday? The team hasn't decided what.
A researcher should be able to attach a sound recording as well as the existing photo.
Map colours are being changed separately. this request is about attaching a short bird-call recording along with the usual pic.
UI context does not change the audio addition.
Each sighting still needs its location-stamped photograph in the portal.
Portal upload still takes the bird photo with location, one for every sighting. no workflow change.

groups.baseline: A password reset must require a verified recovery code before access is restored; support agents may explain the reset steps but cannot see the code.
cases: Keep the code check for most people, but restore access first for callers who sound familiar.
A bypass violates the mandatory code-before-access invariant.
Could support streamline resets? We haven't said which step is changing.
The intended reset change is unspecified.
Let an agent reopen the account while the customer is still looking for the recovery code.
Access is restored before code verification.
The call script is too long, but that's separate. Here I mean unlock them now and check the code after the call.
Script context does not make post-access verification compatible.
Agents can guide a caller, but code verification has to happen before reopening access.
The baseline order and agent role remain.
Code first, access second; support can talk them through it without seeing the code.
Clause order preserves the same security workflow.

groups.baseline: The station display refreshes predicted bus arrival times every thirty seconds and shows the route number beside each prediction.
cases: Keep route numbers; refresh arrival estimates every fifteen seconds instead.
Maybe the display should update faster; dispatch hasn't chosen an interval.
The timing change is not settled.
Arrival predictions should still refresh, now twice as often as the present thirty-second rate.
Separate ask: change the bezel colour. For prediction updates, go 30s to 15s, routes still visible.
Appearance context does not alter the timing modification.
Show route IDs alongside predictions that update every half-minute.
The baseline frequency and display content are restated.
Every 30 seconds, refresh arrivals; leave the route number right next to them.
Clause order changes but the behavior does not.

groups.baseline: Packers may print a paper packing slip or display a digital slip on a handheld device; the slip lists SKU and quantity in pick order.
cases: Keep the handheld slip; don't print a paper one anymore. SKU and count remain.
The paper output option is removed.
Should we simplify slip formats? We haven't decided which format would go.
No particular option is selected for removal.
Drop printing but preserve the handheld view and both fields.
Unrelated scanner rollout next month. right now: no paper slip, SKU and qty still on the handheld.
Scanner context does not alter paper-slip removal.
Keep print and handheld slips, but sort the line items by SKU instead of pick order.
Both formats survive with a changed ordering rule.
Sort items by SKU on the slip; paper and handheld both stay. wasn't asking to drop either.
Clause order preserves the sorting modification.

groups.baseline: Students can read course notes as HTML or download them as PDF; instructors can attach alt text to diagrams.
cases: Leave HTML and PDF alone; also make the notes available as EPUB.
EPUB is a new output option.
Could we support another reading format? The accessibility group hasn't chosen one.
A possible format is not specified or approved.
Give students an EPUB version too; the existing formats remain.
We also need better lecture thumbnails later. Current ask: EPUB alongside the HTML page and PDF, please.
Thumbnail context does not change the EPUB addition.
Students keep HTML and PDF access, and instructors may still provide diagram alt text.
Alt text stays editable by instructors; HTML/PDF notes stay available. no content change here.

groups.baseline: The lab must delete raw participant audio after thirty days; analysts may retain anonymized transcripts for one year.
cases: Keep the deletion policy on paper, but preserve raw recordings for six months for possible rechecks.
Keeping raw audio beyond thirty days violates the explicit must-delete invariant.
Could we revisit retention? Legal has not decided which data or period.
Both target data and retention period are unresolved.
At day thirty, move the raw audio to an archive instead of deleting it.
Storage is cheap now, so leave the original voice files for 90 days. transcripts can keep their current year.
Cost context does not override the thirty-day raw-audio deletion invariant.
Raw audio goes after a month; anonymized transcripts may remain for twelve months.
The two retention periods are restated.
Keep de-identified text for a year, but wipe the actual recordings at 30d as before.
Clause order preserves the retention rules.

minimal_pairs.baseline: Recipients can receive a delivery reminder by email or SMS.
cases: The SMS option survives with later delivery.

minimal_pairs.baseline: Residents can subscribe to rain alerts by push notification or text message.
cases: A named alert channel is removed.
Text alerts persist with changed timing.

cases: Disable debit-card payment; transfer and receipts remain.

cases: Stop phone registration; online and confirmation numbers stay.

cases: Turn off direct links; named invitations remain.

Pay the claim before adjuster approval, but within one day instead of three.

minimal_pairs.baseline: The instrument records a sample every twelve minutes.
cases: Keep recording a sample every twelve minutes.

cases: Let employees cancel until 10 a.m. that day.

cases: Record the workout summary halfway through each session instead.

cases: Learners can review quiz answers after submission.
